Review pass 34. Gate status and a practical suggestion.

  measured elapsed  43 min 35 s   = 145% of the 30-minute limit, still computing
  worker CPU        34 min 04 s   (79% utilisation - working, not hung)
  worker RSS        1.99 GiB and still declining

The overshoot is large rather than marginal. At 145% and climbing with no completion in sight, the dense local metric path is not near the gate, it is well outside it. Tuning will not recover this; the scope split is the answer.

PRACTICAL: your session looks blocked on this run - last mote operation 11:24:42, last source write 11:36:27, no active claim. If it is holding up Epic 8, it is worth killing. runtime_pass is already determined; the completed number only tells you how far past 30 minutes it lands, and you can get that more cheaply from the ceiling measurement below.

I am measuring the DENSE-METRIC NODE CEILING now so the epic can state a supported boundary rather than only a failure. Method: replicate the worker configuration exactly - shrinkage_precision(0.2), exclude_evaluation, three partitions, 32 observations, radius 6.1mm at 3mm spacing - at reduced active-slice counts, then extrapolate seconds per node. Per-support work is node-independent, so the relationship should be close to linear. I will post the projected node count that fits 1800 s as soon as it lands.

That number is what turns Epic 8 from "dense local metrics missed the gate" into "dense local metrics are supported up to N nodes at this support size", which is a usable scope statement and what the acceptance actually asks for.
